posts.content_md:
**A QUASI-SCIENTIFIC ATTEMPT TO UNDERSTAND ALCOHOL-ENHANCED DRYING IN CONJUNCTION WITH TABLE SUGAR POST-SWELL**

Night 1: Copied H1 transmission master on VRP-M glass plate onto reflection H2 VRP-M glass plate.

Beam ratios 1:0.88 (object:reference) - under normal conditions this scenario would result in bright green replay highlighted with gold/red because...

...to combat the humidity in my clime I post-swell with 1 teaspoon table sugar per 150ml wetting agent (Integraf Form-A-Flow/distilled water)

But last night...

Finished up processing with two baths isopropyl alcohol:

Bath 1 - 45% alcohol concentration - ~10 seconds agitation, lift/angle plate 5X to "drag" off water

Bath 1 - 91% alcohol concentration - ~10 seconds agitation, lift/angle plate 5X to "drag" off water

Stand plate on edge on paper towel to dry

Results: Clear image vivid blue in center (where reference beam was strongest), bright green around periphria - NO RED BLOBBIES!!!!!!!!!

General conclusion: Drying with alcohol un-does post swell...

...but to what degree?

Will a higher concentration of sugar make a difference?

Stay tuned to find out!

It sounds to me as though the silver halide part of DJ Mathson's long thread discussion below on this page is relevant to what you are asking, it is primarily aimed for 532nm exposures.

 The conclusion from that thread (so far) is to ditch items such as sugar, sorbitol,glycerine for post- swelling and use citric acid instead.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
I think you missed what glajciorz said. The sugar is disolving out of the emulsion, or actually diluting out, in the alcohol baths. It needs to stay there to "puff" up the fringes. 

I would try to see if sugar is disolvable in pure alcohol. If it is then put your same 1 teaspoon to alcohol/water mixtures. If it does not disolve in alcohol, then put 1 teaspoon per the water volume in you alcohol/water mixtures.

Yes officially sugar is not supposed to be soluable in 100% alcohol so the observations are a bit puzzling. 

However Justin should put that on one side forget the sugar and go and get some citric acid from local drug store and use that. Provided he dries with near 100% alcohol the citric acid will stay combined in the gelatin layer and "puff it up" as you put it and replay at longer wavelength. See pics from Paulos (accidentally ascribed to "ascorbic "rather than citric acid)

[http://www.holographyforum.org/phpBB2/v ... sc&start=0](http://www.holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=5224&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=0)

posts.author: Justin W
posts.content_md:
Kool, kool, kool.

Citric acid sounds like the post-swell of choice!

I can dig it.

But the thing is... I shouldn't need to be manipulating my color at all - I'm shooting on green-sensitive film with a green laser! I can state for a fact that the infernal blueness of my images is not the result of abysmal beam ratios. My exposure techniques are solid (albeit somewhat ghetto). Nope nope nope. VRP-M should have a natural green replay color. That would suit me just fine. Frikkin Florida just won't give up on this rainy season and must be pre-swelling my emulsion, leading to blue replay from a green exposure. Which brings me around to...

...ORIGINAL POST UPDATE:

Last I mentioned my alcohol-related foibles, I stated intent to undo the high-ambient-humidity-pre-swell with an alcohol bath shortly before exposure. This was a losing gamble. The alcohol pre-bath seems to have hyper-sensitized my emulsion (plate developed solid black in the blink of an eye), and wasn't even a hologram after drying. Like a step back in time to my early days of this crap - Where's my image? I know that the reference beam did a lot of exposing because of how dark and uniform the plate was, but the final "hologram" acts like it was exposed with object beam (H1 replay) only.... Puzzling and eery and frankly, a little disconcerting.

ANYWAY... That didn't work, and with my goal being to have my VRP-M act like VRP-M should, perhaps it's time to nip this in the bud and work on storage techniques that don't allow this humidity to ruin my plates before I can get a chance to do so for myself 

So I'll wrap things up like this: If post-swell returns to my wanna-do list, citric acid is the thing to try. Thanks to all who have labored so intensely to bring this to my attention.

Next then: How do I store my VRP-M glass plates so that the humidity doesn't effect their normal behavior? I imagine the fridge would be cool - EXCEPT - I cringe at the thought of pulling a plate from the fridge only to watch it sweat like a cold pepsi can.

And while we're off-topic: Please note that I will be starting a new post wherein I beg, grovel and plead for some assistance in getting a spatial filter integrated successfully into my setup 8)

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
Have you tried washing the film in normal water and drying? Or better, pre-soak in 4% TEA, then wash in DI and dry.

I found that if I don't pre-wash Filmotec material, I get a blue shift. But if I pre-wash I don't. Perhaps the pre-wash removes stuff that's in the VRP film to prevent it from spoiling.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
It might not be humidity that's affecting your final color. If I remember correctly you're using a dichromate bleach which will remove material during bleaching. This will cause the emulsion to shrink and shift your replay color toward blue.

What hans brings up may be true as well and the combination of the two will result in more shifting.
